newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks look to bumper results crop next week.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks look to bumper results crop next week.

text.p: A heavy flow of results from major companies should provide the focus of attention for the UK equity market next week, with eight firms in the blue chip FTSE 100 index due to report in the next five trading sessions.
Yet after a week in which UK shares have been buffeted by fears of rising UK interest rates, analysts said the market remains vulnerable to further signs that rates may rise again in the near future.

The FTSE 100 dropped to its lowest intraday level for two months last week before ending on a firm note, underpinned by rising bonds and further record peaks on Wall Street, where shares were still enjoying a post-election surge.

Nick Glydon, chart analyst at Robert Fleming Securities, said strength in bond markets and overseas stock markets could continue to insulate the FTSE from worries over the deteriorating domestic outlook.
"The FTSE has proved very resilient," Glydon said. "Bond markets have been looking strong and U.S. and continental markets have been going to record levels."
"The UK has a high correlation to Wall Street and if everything else is going up we are not going to come down."
Friday's weaker-than-expected U.S. economic reports, showing a surprise 0.5 percent drop in October industrial output, again buoyed U.S. markets and pushed UK shares higher.
Yet UK figures have not been so market-friendly and Thursday's rise in the UK's underlying inflation rate to a higher-than-expected 3.3 percent is likely to continue to dog shares here.
Analysts said the FTSE index, which has declined from its record 4,073.2 on October 21, may need to break solidly above 3,950 to cement a new upswing.
"The market is still looking a bit nervous," said Glydon.

UK rates have already been raised a quarter point to dampen growth and ward off inflation pressures, and there are concerns that rates may be raised again before Christmas if the run of strong economic pointers continues.
Prospects of high inflation through 1997, and an election which must be held by next May, are enough to persuade some strategists that UK shares are likely to remain under pressure.
"We are still concerned about the UK market," said Mike Young, European strategist at Goldman Sachs. "My best guess is that 12 months from now the index won't be far different from where it is now."
Next week's key UK economic report is October retail sales on Wednesday, expected to show a 0.5 percent rise in October from the month before, lifting the annual rate of increase to 4.1 percent.
Other economic reports include the final estimate for GDP growth in third quarter, with yearly growth originally put at a relatively robust 2.3 percent.
In the U.S. it is a relatively thin week for economic reports, the main release being the Philidelphia Fed report of regional economic trends.

UK companies reporting in the week include industrial gases group BOC Group Plc, music publisher EMI Group Plc, mobile phone company Vodafone Group Plc, telecoms group Cable & Wireless Plc, chemicals group Courtaulds Plc, media and leisure firm Granada Group Plc, power generator National Power Plc and supermarket group Safeway Plc.
